title: Geometric data for smooth purity exchange
statement: Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, an integer $a\ge1$, an algebraic closure $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_{p^a}$, and a fixed coefficient closure as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X,X',Y,Y'$ be schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $f:X\to Y$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ be morphisms, and let $d\ge0$ be an integer. Define $\operatorname{Geometry}(f,f',d)$ to be the bundle of the following data: each of the four schemes $W$ is Noetherian (quasi-compact and covered by affine spectra of Noetherian rings); for each $W$ there exists $n_W\in\mathbf N$ with $\dim W\le n_W$, with topological Krull dimension as in [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; $\ell$ is a unit in every stalk $\mathcal O_{W,w}$; $f$ and $f'$ are locally of finite type and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; $f'$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and smooth of pure relative dimension $d$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. This definition does not assert existence of the bundle or impose a Cartesian-square hypothesis. For any $k$-scheme $W$ and point $w\in W$, also define $\operatorname{finiteResidueInverse}(W,w)$ as the multiplicative-invertibility datum for $\ell$ in $\kappa(w)$ [def-weil-residue-field], obtained by mapping its coefficient-convention unit in $\mathcal O_{W,w}$ through the residue map; it uses the same field and coefficient data. The inverse is uniquely determined by the two inverse identities. In applications to smooth-exchange squares the bundle is supplied as a conclusion. All schemes and fields use the universe of the purity conventions.
